notes: Access: same intermittent PerimeterX behaviour as documented for Bestsellers/New Arrivals on this company -- eventually got through on all needed requests with curl_cffi profile brute-forcing + retries; robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow. Thorough check for a genuine Clearance/Outlet PLP: (1) the site's top-level mega-nav has no 'Clearance'/'Outlet'/'Final Sale'/'Last Chance'/'Closeout'/'End of Line' department -- the only sale-labelled top-nav item is 'Sale', linking to https://www.wayfair.co.uk/daily-sales, a pure BlockBuilderCuratedNavigation hub (no H1, no resultCount, no product grid of its own) that fans out to ~50 temporary/curated tiles named things like 'Our Top Sofas', 'Top Rated Dining Chairs', 'Bargains under £50', 'Sales by Department', 'Blankets: Best Picks' -- none use Clearance/Outlet/Final Sale/Last Chance/Closeout/End of Line/Discontinued wording anywhere in their titles; (2) the seo-category-sitemap (513 URLs) contains only per-category '<name>-sale-c<id>.html' pages (e.g. 'home-decor-sale', 'wall-art-sale') -- these are ordinary percent-off category filters under the generic 'Sale' banner, not a site-defined Clearance/Outlet taxonomy node, and carry no permanence signal, so excluded per the Sale-vs-Clearance rule; (3) the seo-sb1 sitemap's few 'clearance'/'outlet' URL hits are false positives -- product-attribute filters (e.g. 'low-clearance-under-8-in-beds', 'built-in-outlet-floor-lamps') or a garden-furniture brand literally named 'Furniture Outlet Ltd', not merchandising pages; (4) tried the same search-redirect trick that surfaced a genuine 'Closeout' curated event page on this project's Joss & Main pass (same Wayfair-family platform): fetched /keyword.php?keyword=clearance, =outlet, =closeout, ="final sale", ="last chance" directly. Unlike Joss & Main, every one of these resolved to a generic pageType 'KeywordSearch' page (large/round hit counts of 2528, 6000-capped, 1900 and 3985 respectively, no eventRoadsign, no curated taxonomy, title just 'Clearance | Wayfair.co.uk' etc. -- ordinary keyword-match results, not a merchandising PLP), except 'outlet', which literally server-redirected (pageType 'DailySalesMainPage', currentURL '.../daily-sales?redir=outlet&rtype=7') straight back to the generic Sale hub, i.e. the platform's own fallback for a keyword with no dedicated page. Also confirmed the ~48 'Clearance' string hits found on every fetched page are all the same per-SKU/variant GraphQL field 'clearanceFulfillment' (fulfillment-source metadata on individual listings), not a page-level Clearance concept -- same as documented for sibling Birch Lane. Conclusion: this Wayfair-family sibling does NOT reproduce the search-redirect-to-curated-event trick that worked on Joss & Main; wayfair.co.uk has no genuine Clearance/Outlet-type merchandising PLP as of this pass. No ambiguous Sale-labelled listing was found that warranted a MANUAL REVIEW flag -- every candidate was either a clear generic temporary promotion/percent-off filter or a plain keyword-search page with no clearance-taxonomy signal.
